newsitem.title: PANAMA: SOCCER-NINE-MAN CANADA DRAW TO REACH FINAL QUALIFYING ROUND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NINE-MAN CANADA DRAW TO REACH FINAL QUALIFYING ROUND.

text.p: Canada had two players sent off but still managed to hold on for a scoreless draw in a World Cup qualifying match with Panama on Sunday, a result that put them in the final round of the CONCACAF qualifiers.
Panama, which dominated the match, also had a player dismissed in a rough, bad-tempered clash.
Canada goalkeeper Craig Forrest, in possession of the ball at the time, was shown the red card in the 82nd minute for kicking Panama's Neftal Diaz.
Twenty minutes earlier Paul Peschisolido of Canada and Rolando Botello of Panama had also been sent off for fighting.

Panama, with an attack spearheaded by French-based striker Julio Cesar Dely Valdez and his brother Jorge, created numerous chances and had a penalty appeal turned down but were unable to find a way post Forrest.
The draw was good enough to give Canada a top-two finish in the semifinal stage in group two, giving it a berth in the final stage of the CONCACAF qualifiers.
Panama is in last place but could still go through by winning their last two matches with some help from other results in the group.
Six teams will take part in the final CONCACAF qualifying round with the top three earning places in the 1998 World Cup.
